steps.action: Opened Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps in the project browser profile (owner already signed in)
steps.observation: Signed in already, no re-authentication, 2FA, CAPTCHA or email prompt appeared (whether the email was already verified was not checked). The OAuth Apps list was empty.

steps.action: Clicked New OAuth app and read the registration form
steps.observation: Form fields: name*, homepage URL*, description (optional), Redirect URIs (up to 10, wildcard option), Enable Device Flow, Expire user access tokens (ticked by default).

steps.action: Filled the form with throwaway values (oauthpath-test-20261029, http://localhost:3000, http://localhost:3000/callback) and clicked Register application
steps.observation: GitHub reported 'Application created successfully' and opened the app settings page. No terms to accept, no payment, no review step appeared.

steps.action: Read the new app's settings page without generating a secret
steps.observation: A Client ID is shown at once. The page says a client secret is needed and offers 'Generate a new client secret'; none was generated, to keep secrets out of logs.

steps.action: Cleanup: the owner clicked Delete application in the Danger zone; the agent reloaded the OAuth Apps list
steps.observation: The list showed 'No OAuth apps' afterwards. A first delete attempt had not taken effect, and a second one did.

stoppedAt: the client-secret step (guide step 4): no secret was generated; steps 5 to 7 were not attempted

corrections.docClaim: An Authorization callback URL that you own and control, since ownership of it prevents token leakage to an attacker.
corrections.observed: The form labels it 'Redirect URIs': up to 10 are allowed, with an optional wildcard-matching checkbox. The label 'Authorization callback URL' was not shown.

corrections.docClaim: Access tokens can expire after eight hours with a refresh token that expires after six months without use. Requesting offline_access opts in per sign-in. Existing non-expiring tokens are not changed when expiry is later enforced.
corrections.observed: The registration form has 'Expire user access tokens' ticked by default, which provides refresh tokens. The offline_access scope was not tested.

corrections.docClaim: The app gets a unique Client ID and Client Secret.
corrections.observed: The Client ID is shown at once; a client secret is created only after clicking 'Generate a new client secret'.
